name: certification
description: What a standard is made of: a criterion names the rules that judge one thing about a subject and what it measures; a level is a use the subject may be put to, requires criteria, and says what reaching it allows. A certificate (quern.certify) is run from these two kinds and the rules a standard's own package carries, so a standard improves by republishing, with no reader changed.

vocabulary.description: One thing a standard judges about a subject. Payload: `applies_to` (the kind of node it judges, or several), `rules` (the names of the rules that judge it) and `measures` (what it is a measure of, in the standard's own word: completeness, reliability, consistency, presentation). Held when every rule it names holds on the subject and beneath it. Payload `say`, per language, is its name for people.

A use a subject may be put to. Payload: `of` (the kind of subject) and `allows` (what reaching it opens, as the names its readers ask by: a document shown, an entry shared; may be empty); the link `requires` to the criteria that use needs. Reached when every criterion it requires is held. Payload `say`, per language, is its name for people.

rules.name: a-criterion-names-what-it-judges
rules.description: A criterion names the kind of node it judges, the rules that judge it, and what it measures.

fr.red: Ce critère ne dit pas ce qu'il juge, par quelles règles, ou ce qu'il mesure.

en.red: This criterion does not say what it judges, by which rules, or what it measures.

rules.name: a-level-requires-criteria
rules.expr: len(payload(self, 'of', '')) > 0 and len(linked(self, 'requires')) > 0 and every(c, linked(self, 'requires'), some(k, nodes('criterion'), k == c))
rules.description: A level says the kind of subject it is a use of and requires criteria that exist.

fr.red: Ce niveau ne dit pas de quoi il est un usage, ou exige un critère qui n'existe pas.

en.red: This level does not say what it is a use of, or requires a criterion that does not exist.

counter_examples.because: a criterion that names no rule judges nothing
a level requiring a criterion that does not exist
